title: Shared Inbox for Small Support Teams — Jon Martin

blocks.html: This is for a team of two to ten people answering customer email from a shared address, usually by forwarding and cc'ing each other, and losing track of who replied.
Many of these teams also keep customers in HubSpot. The question is whether support conversations need to sit on that record, or whether a separate inbox is fine.

Pick SupportBee if you want a plain shared inbox at the lowest per-seat price. Pick Help Scout if you want to start on a free plan and grow into chat and a help center. Pick Front if the team lives in email and you want HubSpot contacts and deals visible beside each thread.
For a three-person team billed annually, that's about $51 a month on SupportBee Startup, and about $75 on Front Starter.

SupportBee Startup is $17 per seat per month billed annually ($204 per seat a year). Enterprise is $21 per seat per month billed annually ($252 per seat a year). Per SupportBee, annual billing saves 20%. Plans include unlimited email inboxes and tickets, and Startup comes with 1 knowledge base and 1 team. There's a 14-day free trial.
It's the most focused of the three: a shared inbox, a knowledge base, and the basics around them, without a long list of channels to configure.

Help Scout has a free plan with 5 users, 1 inbox, and 1 Docs site. Standard is $25 per user per month as shown on the pricing page’s default view, and it includes multiple inboxes, plus live chat and SMS. Plus is $45 per user per month as shown on the default view, adding Salesforce, Jira, and HubSpot integrations. Plus also allows teammates who view and collaborate without a full seat, up to 25.
Check the monthly and annual toggle on Help Scout's pricing page before you budget, since the figures above are what the default view shows.

Front Starter is $25 per seat per month billed annually, up to 10 seats. Professional is $65 per seat per month billed annually, up to 50 seats. Per Front, annual billing saves 24%. Starter gives you shared inbox and ticketing, with up to 10 automation rules. There's a 14-day free trial of Professional features, no credit card.
On HubSpot, Front offers an integration with HubSpot CRM, so contacts and deals sit next to conversations. That's the pick for a team that works deals and support out of the same inbox.
Start with seats. Count everyone who needs to reply, not everyone who needs to read. Some plans let teammates view without a full seat, and that changes the bill.
Then decide if support history belongs in HubSpot. If sales needs to see open tickets before a renewal call, a direct HubSpot connection is worth paying for. If not, keep it simple.
Last, look at the ceiling. Seat caps, automation rule limits, and knowledge base counts are what push a small team onto the next plan.
Write down three rules first: who owns a new email, how fast you reply, and when a thread counts as done. The tool enforces rules; it doesn't invent them.
Move one address at a time, and keep the old inbox forwarding for a few weeks so nothing slips through.

closing: Agree on who owns each email first, then pick the cheapest inbox that enforces it and reaches HubSpot if you need it to.
